passages.text: Now in the church at Antioch there were prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen (who had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch), and Saul.
passages.sermon:
The church was in Antioch.
This church had prophets and teachers.
Barnabas was one of them.
Simeon was also there.
People called Simeon Niger.
Lucius was there too.
Lucius came from Cyrene.
Manaen was also present.
Manaen grew up with Herod the tetrarch.
Saul was there as well.
passages.original: Ἦσαν δὲ ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ κατὰ τὴν οὖσαν ἐκκλησίαν προφῆται καὶ διδάσκαλοι ὅ τε Βαρνάβας καὶ Συμεὼν ὁ καλούμενος Νίγερ καὶ Λούκιος ὁ Κυρηναῖος Μαναήν τε Ἡρῴδου τοῦ τετραάρχου σύντροφος καὶ Σαῦλος

passages.text: While they were worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, “Set apart for Me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.”
passages.sermon:
Barnabas, Simeon called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen, and Saul were in the church at Antioch.
They were prophets and teachers.
They worshiped the Lord.
They fasted.
The Holy Spirit spoke to them.
The Holy Spirit said, “Set apart Barnabas and Saul for Me.”
The Holy Spirit had called Barnabas and Saul to a special work.
passages.original: Λειτουργούντων δὲ αὐτῶν τῷ Κυρίῳ καὶ νηστευόντων εἶπεν τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον Ἀφορίσατε δή μοι τὸν Βαρνάβαν καὶ Σαῦλον εἰς τὸ ἔργον ὃ προσκέκλημαι αὐτούς

passages.text: And after they had fasted and prayed, they laid their hands on them and sent them off.
passages.sermon:
The believers in the church at Antioch fasted.
They prayed.
They laid their hands on Barnabas and Saul.
They sent Barnabas and Saul off.
passages.original: τότε νηστεύσαντες καὶ προσευξάμενοι καὶ ἐπιθέντες τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῖς ἀπέλυσαν

passages.text: So Barnabas and Saul, sent forth by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia and sailed from there to Cyprus.
passages.sermon: Barnabas and Saul were sent by the Holy Spirit.\r\nThey went down to Seleucia.\r\nThey sailed from Seleucia to Cyprus.
passages.original: Αὐτοὶ μὲν οὖν ἐκπεμφθέντες ὑπὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος κατῆλθον εἰς Σελεύκειαν ἐκεῖθέν τε ἀπέπλευσαν εἰς Κύπρον

passages.text: When they arrived at Salamis, they proclaimed the word of God in the Jewish synagogues. And John was with them as their helper.
passages.sermon:
Barnabas and Saul arrived at Salamis.
They went to the Jewish synagogues.
They proclaimed the word of God there.
John was with them.
John served as their helper.
passages.original: καὶ γενόμενοι ἐν Σαλαμῖνι κατήγγελλον τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς τῶν Ἰουδαίων εἶχον δὲ καὶ Ἰωάννην ὑπηρέτην

passages.text: They traveled through the whole island as far as Paphos, where they found a Jewish sorcerer and false prophet named Bar-Jesus, an attendant of the proconsul, Sergius Paulus. The proconsul, a man of intelligence, summoned Barnabas and Saul because he wanted to hear the word of God.
passages.sermon:
Barnabas and Saul traveled through the whole island of Cyprus.
They went as far as the city of Paphos.
In Paphos, they found a man named Bar-Jesus.
Bar-Jesus was a Jew.
He was a sorcerer.
He was also a false prophet.
Bar-Jesus stayed with the proconsul.
The proconsul’s name was Sergius Paulus.
Sergius Paulus was a Roman official.
He was a man of intelligence.
Sergius Paulus called for Barnabas and Saul.
He wanted to hear the word of God from them.
passages.original: Διελθόντες δὲ ὅλην τὴν νῆσον ἄχρι Πάφου εὗρον ἄνδρα τινὰ μάγον ψευδοπροφήτην Ἰουδαῖον ᾧ ὄνομα Βαριησοῦ ὃς ἦν σὺν τῷ ἀνθυπάτῳ Σεργίῳ Παύλῳ ἀνδρὶ συνετῷ οὗτος προσκαλεσάμενος Βαρνάβαν καὶ Σαῦλον ἐπεζήτησεν ἀκοῦσαι τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: But Elymas the sorcerer (for that is what his name means) opposed them and tried to turn the proconsul from the faith.
passages.sermon:
Elymas was a sorcerer.
His name means "sorcerer."
Elymas opposed Barnabas and Saul.
He tried to turn the proconsul away from the faith.
passages.original: ἀνθίστατο δὲ αὐτοῖς Ἐλύμας ὁ μάγος οὕτως γὰρ μεθερμηνεύεται τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ζητῶν διαστρέψαι τὸν ἀνθύπατον ἀπὸ τῆς πίστεως

passages.text: Then Saul, who was also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, looked directly at Elymas and said, “O child of the devil and enemy of all righteousness, you are full of all kinds of deceit and trickery! Will you never stop perverting the straight ways of the Lord?
passages.sermon:
Saul was also called Paul.
Paul was filled with the Holy Spirit.
Paul looked directly at Elymas.
Paul spoke to Elymas.
Paul said, “You are full of all kinds of deceit and trickery.
You are a child of the devil.
You are an enemy of all righteousness.
You keep perverting the straight ways of the Lord.
Will you never stop doing this?”
passages.original: Σαῦλος δέ ὁ καὶ Παῦλος πλησθεὶς Πνεύματος Ἁγίου ἀτενίσας εἰς αὐτὸν εἶπεν Ὦ πλήρης παντὸς δόλου καὶ πάσης ῥᾳδιουργίας υἱὲ διαβόλου ἐχθρὲ πάσης δικαιοσύνης οὐ παύσῃ διαστρέφων τὰς ὁδοὺς τοῦ Κυρίου τὰς εὐθείας

passages.text: Now look, the hand of the Lord is against you, and for a time you will be blind and unable to see the light of the sun.” Immediately mist and darkness came over him, and he groped about, seeking someone to lead him by the hand.
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke to Elymas the sorcerer.
Paul was filled with the Holy Spirit.
Paul said, “Now the hand of the Lord is against you.
You will be blind for a time.
You will not see the light of the sun.”
Immediately, mist and darkness came over Elymas.
Elymas became blind.
He walked around, searching for someone to lead him by the hand.
passages.original: καὶ νῦν ἰδοὺ χεὶρ Κυρίου ἐπὶ σέ καὶ ἔσῃ τυφλὸς μὴ βλέπων τὸν ἥλιον ἄχρι καιροῦ παραχρῆμα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἀχλὺς καὶ σκότος καὶ περιάγων ἐζήτει χειραγωγούς

passages.text: When the proconsul saw what had happened, he believed, for he was astonished at the teaching about the Lord.
passages.sermon: The proconsul saw what happened.\r\nHe believed.\r\nHe was astonished at the teaching about the Lord.
passages.original: Τότε ἰδὼν ὁ ἀνθύπατος τὸ γεγονὸς ἐπίστευσεν ἐκπλησσόμενος ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ τοῦ Κυρίου

passages.text: After setting sail from Paphos, Paul and his companions came to Perga in Pamphylia, where John left them to return to Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Paul had several companions.
They set sail from Paphos.
They arrived at Perga in the region of Pamphylia.
John was with them.
John left Paul and the others.
John returned to Jerusalem.
passages.original: Ἀναχθέντες δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς Πάφου οἱ περὶ Παῦλον ἦλθον εἰς Πέργην τῆς Παμφυλίας Ἰωάννης δὲ ἀποχωρήσας ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ὑπέστρεψεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα

passages.text: And from Perga, they traveled inland to Pisidian Antioch, where they entered the synagogue on the Sabbath and sat down.
passages.sermon:
Paul and his companions left Perga.
They traveled to Pisidian Antioch.
They entered the synagogue in Pisidian Antioch on the Sabbath.
They sat down in the synagogue.
passages.original: Αὐτοὶ δὲ διελθόντες ἀπὸ τῆς Πέργης παρεγένοντο εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν τὴν Πισιδίαν καὶ εἰσελθόντες εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῶν σαββάτων ἐκάθισαν

passages.text: After the reading from the Law and the Prophets, the synagogue leaders sent word to them: “Brothers, if you have a word of encouragement for the people, please speak.”
passages.sermon:
Paul and his companions visited a synagogue in Pisidian Antioch on the Sabbath.
The people read from the Law and the Prophets.
The synagogue leaders spoke to Paul and his companions.
They sent a message to them.
They said, “Brothers, if you have a word of encouragement for the people, please speak.”
passages.original: μετὰ δὲ τὴν ἀνάγνωσιν τοῦ νόμου καὶ τῶν προφητῶν ἀπέστειλαν οἱ ἀρχισυνάγωγοι πρὸς αὐτοὺς λέγοντες Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί εἴ τίς ἐστιν ἐν ὑμῖν λόγος παρακλήσεως πρὸς τὸν λαόν λέγετε

passages.text: Paul stood up, motioned with his hand, and began to speak: “Men of Israel and you Gentiles who fear God, listen to me!
passages.sermon:
Paul was present in the synagogue at Antioch in Pisidia.
Paul stood up.
Paul motioned with his hand.
Paul began to speak.
Paul addressed the men of Israel.
Paul also addressed the Gentiles who feared God.
Paul said, "Listen to me."
passages.original: Ἀναστὰς δὲ Παῦλος καὶ κατασείσας τῇ χειρὶ εἶπεν Ἄνδρες Ἰσραηλῖται καὶ οἱ φοβούμενοι τὸν Θεόν ἀκούσατε

passages.text: The God of the people of Israel chose our fathers. He made them into a great people during their stay in Egypt, and with an uplifted arm He led them out of that land.
passages.sermon:
The God of the people of Israel acted with power.
He chose our fathers.
He made our fathers into a great people.
He did this while they lived in Egypt.
He led them out of Egypt with a mighty arm.
passages.original: ὁ Θεὸς τοῦ λαοῦ τούτου Ἰσραὴλ ἐξελέξατο τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν καὶ τὸν λαὸν ὕψωσεν ἐν τῇ παροικίᾳ ἐν γῇ Αἰγύπτου καὶ μετὰ βραχίονος ὑψηλοῦ ἐξήγαγεν αὐτοὺς ἐξ αὐτῆς

passages.text: He endured their conduct for about forty years in the wilderness.
passages.sermon:
God showed patience to the people of Israel.
He endured their behavior.
He did this for about forty years.
This happened while they were in the wilderness.
passages.original: καί ὡς τεσσερακονταετῆ χρόνον ἐτροποφόρησεν αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ

passages.text: And having vanquished seven nations in Canaan, He gave their land to His people as an inheritance.
passages.sermon:
God acted for the people of Israel.
God defeated seven nations in the land of Canaan.
God gave the land of these nations to His people.
God made this land their inheritance.
passages.original: καὶ καθελὼν ἔθνη ἑπτὰ ἐν γῇ Χανάαν κατεκληρονόμησεν τὴν γῆν αὐτῶν

passages.text: All this took about 450 years. After this, God gave them judges until the time of Samuel the prophet.
passages.sermon:
God acted for about 450 years.
He did these things during that time.
After this period, God gave Israel judges.
The judges led Israel.
This continued until Samuel became the prophet.
passages.original: ὡς ἔτεσιν τετρακοσίοις καὶ πεντήκοντα Καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἔδωκεν κριτὰς ἕως Σαμουὴλ τοῦ προφήτου

passages.text: Then the people asked for a king, and God gave them forty years under Saul son of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel asked for a king.
God answered their request.
God gave them Saul as king.
Saul was the son of Kish.
Saul came from the tribe of Benjamin.
Saul ruled as king for forty years.
passages.original: κἀκεῖθεν ᾐτήσαντο βασιλέα καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Θεὸς τὸν Σαοὺλ υἱὸν Κίς ἄνδρα ἐκ φυλῆς Βενιαμίν ἔτη τεσσεράκοντα

passages.text: After removing Saul, He raised up David as their king and testified about him: ‘I have found David son of Jesse a man after My own heart; he will carry out My will in its entirety.’
passages.sermon:
God removed Saul from being king.
God then made David their king.
God spoke about David.
God said, “I have found David, son of Jesse.”
David is a man who seeks what I desire.
David will do everything I want.
David will obey all my will.
passages.original: καὶ μεταστήσας αὐτὸν ἤγειρεν τὸν Δαυὶδ αὐτοῖς εἰς βασιλέα ᾧ καὶ εἶπεν μαρτυρήσας Εὗρον Δαυὶδ τὸν τοῦ Ἰεσσαί ἄνδρα κατὰ τὴν καρδίαν μου ὃς ποιήσει πάντα τὰ θελήματά μου

passages.text: From the descendants of this man, God has brought to Israel the Savior Jesus, as He promised.
passages.sermon:
God made a promise.
God kept His promise.
God chose David.
God brought a Savior from David’s descendants.
God gave this Savior to Israel.
This Savior is Jesus.
passages.original: Τούτου ὁ Θεὸς ἀπὸ τοῦ σπέρματος κατ’ ἐπαγγελίαν ἤγαγεν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ Σωτῆρα Ἰησοῦν

passages.text: Before the arrival of Jesus, John preached a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.
passages.sermon:
John was a prophet.
\r\nJohn came before Jesus arrived.
\r\nJohn preached to the people of Israel.
\r\nJohn told everyone to repent.
\r\nJohn called all the people of Israel to be baptized.
\r\nJohn preached a baptism that showed repentance.
passages.original: προκηρύξαντος Ἰωάννου πρὸ προσώπου τῆς εἰσόδου αὐτοῦ βάπτισμα μετανοίας παντὶ τῷ λαῷ Ἰσραήλ

passages.text: As John was completing his course, he said, ‘Who do you suppose I am? I am not that One. But He is coming after me whose sandals I am not worthy to untie.’
passages.sermon:
John was a prophet.
John preached to the people of Israel before Jesus arrived.
John completed his work.
John spoke to the people.
John said, "Who do you think I am?"
John said, "I am not the One you are expecting."
John said, "Someone is coming after me."
John said, "I am not worthy to untie the sandals of the One who comes after me."
passages.original: ὡς δὲ ἐπλήρου Ἰωάννης τὸν δρόμον ἔλεγεν Τί ἐμὲ ὑπονοεῖτε εἶναι οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐγώ ἀλλ’ ἰδοὺ ἔρχεται μετ’ ἐμὲ οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἄξιος τὸ ὑπόδημα τῶν ποδῶν λῦσαι

passages.text: Brothers, children of Abraham, and you Gentiles who fear God, it is to us that this message of salvation has been sent.
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke to the people in the synagogue.
He addressed two groups.
The first group was the children of Abraham.
These were the Jewish people.
The second group was the Gentiles who feared God.
These were non-Jews who respected and worshiped God.
Paul said that God sent a message of salvation.
God sent this message to all of them.
This message was for both Jews and God-fearing Gentiles.
passages.original: Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί υἱοὶ γένους Ἀβραὰμ καὶ οἱ ἐν ὑμῖν φοβούμενοι τὸν Θεόν ἡμῖν ὁ λόγος τῆς σωτηρίας ταύτης ἐξαπεστάλη

passages.text: The people of Jerusalem and their rulers did not recognize Jesus, yet in condemning Him they fulfilled the words of the prophets that are read every Sabbath.
passages.sermon:
The people of Jerusalem lived in that city.
Their rulers led them.
These people did not recognize Jesus.
Their rulers also did not recognize Jesus.
Every Sabbath, they heard the words of the prophets read aloud.
They judged Jesus and condemned Him.
By doing this, they fulfilled the words of the prophets.
passages.original: οἱ γὰρ κατοικοῦντες ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες αὐτῶν τοῦτον ἀγνοήσαντες καὶ τὰς φωνὰς τῶν προφητῶν τὰς κατὰ πᾶν σάββατον ἀναγινωσκομένας κρίναντες ἐπλήρωσαν

passages.text: And though they found no ground for a death sentence, they asked Pilate to have Him executed.
passages.sermon: The people of Jerusalem and their rulers judged Jesus.\r\nThey did not find any reason to sentence Him to death.\r\nThey asked Pilate to put Jesus to death.
passages.original: καὶ μηδεμίαν αἰτίαν θανάτου εὑρόντες ᾐτήσαντο Πιλᾶτον ἀναιρεθῆναι αὐτόν

passages.text: When they had carried out all that was written about Him, they took Him down from the tree and laid Him in a tomb.
passages.sermon:
The people of Jerusalem and their rulers did not recognize Jesus.
They condemned Jesus.
They fulfilled everything written about Jesus.
They took Jesus down from the cross.
They placed Jesus in a tomb.
passages.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐτέλεσαν πάντα τὰ περὶ αὐτοῦ γεγραμμένα καθελόντες ἀπὸ τοῦ ξύλου ἔθηκαν εἰς μνημεῖον

passages.text: But God raised Him from the dead, and for many days He was seen by those who had accompanied Him from Galilee to Jerusalem. They are now His witnesses to our people.
passages.sermon:
God raised Jesus from the dead.
Many people saw Jesus alive for many days.
These people had traveled with Jesus from Galilee to Jerusalem.
Now these people are witnesses for Jesus.
They tell our people what they saw.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ Θεὸς ἤγειρεν αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν ὃς ὤφθη ἐπὶ ἡμέρας πλείους τοῖς συναναβᾶσιν αὐτῷ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ οἵτινες νῦν εἰσιν μάρτυρες αὐτοῦ πρὸς τὸν λαόν

passages.text: And now we proclaim to you the good news: What God promised our fathers He has fulfilled for us, their children, by raising up Jesus. As it is written in the second Psalm: ‘You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.’
passages.sermon:
We now speak to you.
We bring you good news.
God made a promise to our fathers.
God has kept this promise for us, their children.
God fulfilled this promise by raising up Jesus.
The second Psalm says this about Jesus.
God says, “You are My Son.”
God says, “Today I have become Your Father.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἡμεῖς ὑμᾶς εὐαγγελιζόμεθα τὴν πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας ἐπαγγελίαν γενομένην ὅτι ταύτην ὁ Θεὸς ἐκπεπλήρωκεν τοῖς τέκνοις αὐτῶν ἡμῶν ἀναστήσας Ἰησοῦν ὡς καὶ ἐν τῷ ψαλμῷ γέγραπται τῷ δευτέρῳ Υἱός μου εἶ σύ ἐγὼ σήμερον γεγέννηκά σε

passages.text: In fact, God raised Him from the dead, never to see decay. As He has said: ‘I will give you the holy and sure blessings promised to David.’
passages.sermon:
God raised Jesus from the dead.
Jesus will never return to decay.
God said this clearly.
God said, “I will give you the holy and sure blessings promised to David.”
passages.original: Ὅτι δὲ ἀνέστησεν αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν μηκέτι μέλλοντα ὑποστρέφειν εἰς διαφθοράν οὕτως εἴρηκεν ὅτι Δώσω ὑμῖν τὰ ὅσια Δαυὶδ τὰ πιστά

passages.text: So also, He says in another Psalm: ‘You will not let Your Holy One see decay.’
passages.sermon:
God speaks in another Psalm.
God says, “You will not let your Holy One see decay.”
God promises that His Holy One will not experience corruption.
God’s words show that His chosen one will not undergo decay.
passages.original: Διότι καὶ ἐν ἑτέρῳ λέγει Οὐ δώσεις τὸν Ὅσιόν σου ἰδεῖν διαφθοράν

passages.text: For when David had served God’s purpose in his own generation, he fell asleep. His body was buried with his fathers and saw decay.
passages.sermon:
David was a king of Israel.
\r\nDavid served God’s purpose during his own lifetime.
\r\nAfter David finished his service, he died.
\r\nPeople buried David with his ancestors.
\r\nDavid’s body saw decay.
passages.original: Δαυὶδ μὲν γὰρ ἰδίᾳ γενεᾷ ὑπηρετήσας τῇ τοῦ Θεοῦ βουλῇ ἐκοιμήθη καὶ προσετέθη πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας αὐτοῦ καὶ εἶδεν διαφθοράν

passages.text: But the One whom God raised from the dead did not see decay.
passages.sermon: God raised Jesus from the dead.\r\nJesus did not see decay.
passages.original: ὃν δὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἤγειρεν οὐκ εἶδεν διαφθοράν

passages.text: Therefore let it be known to you, brothers, that through Jesus the forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you.
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke to the people in the synagogue.
Paul called them brothers.
Paul wanted them to know something important.
God sent Jesus.
Through Jesus, God offers forgiveness of sins.
Paul proclaimed this message to them.
passages.original: Γνωστὸν οὖν ἔστω ὑμῖν ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί ὅτι διὰ τούτου ὑμῖν ἄφεσις ἁμαρτιῶν καταγγέλλεται

passages.text: Through Him everyone who believes is justified from everything you could not be justified from by the law of Moses.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the one God raised from the dead.
Jesus did not see decay.
God gives forgiveness of sins through Jesus.
Everyone who believes in Jesus is justified.
The law of Moses could not justify you from everything.
Jesus justifies you from all things the law could not.
Belief in Jesus brings this justification.
passages.original: καὶ ἀπὸ πάντων ὧν οὐκ ἠδυνήθητε ἐν νόμῳ Μωϋσέως δικαιωθῆναι ἐν τούτῳ πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων δικαιοῦται

passages.text: Watch out, then, that what was spoken by the prophets does not happen to you: ‘Look, you scoffers, wonder and perish! For I am doing a work in your days that you would never believe, even if someone told you.’”
passages.sermon:
Paul warned the people in the synagogue.
He spoke to Jews and devout converts to Judaism.
He told them to be careful.
He said, "Do not let what the prophets said happen to you."
The prophets spoke about scoffers.
They said, "Look, you scoffers."
They said, "Be amazed and perish."
God said, "I am doing a work in your days."
God said, "You will not believe this work."
God said, "You will not believe it even if someone tells you about it."
passages.original: βλέπετε οὖν μὴ ἐπέλθῃ τὸ εἰρημένον ἐν τοῖς προφήταις Ἴδετε οἱ καταφρονηταί καὶ θαυμάσατε καὶ ἀφανίσθητε ὅτι ἔργον ἐργάζομαι ἐγὼ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ὑμῶν ἔργον ὃ οὐ μὴ πιστεύσητε ἐάν τις ἐκδιηγῆται ὑμῖν

passages.text: As Paul and Barnabas were leaving the synagogue, the people urged them to continue this message on the next Sabbath.
passages.sermon:
Paul and Barnabas were leaving the synagogue.
The people spoke to Paul and Barnabas.
The people asked them to speak these words again.
The people wanted to hear this message on the next Sabbath.
passages.original: Ἐξιόντων δὲ αὐτῶν παρεκάλουν εἰς τὸ μεταξὺ σάββατον λαληθῆναι αὐτοῖς τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα

passages.text: After the synagogue was dismissed, many of the Jews and devout converts to Judaism followed Paul and Barnabas, who spoke to them and urged them to continue in the grace of God.
passages.sermon:
The synagogue meeting ended.
Many Jews left the synagogue.
Many devout converts to Judaism also left.
These Jews and converts followed Paul and Barnabas.
Paul and Barnabas spoke to them.
Paul and Barnabas urged them.
They told them to continue in the grace of God.
passages.original: λυθείσης δὲ τῆς συναγωγῆς ἠκολούθησαν πολλοὶ τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ τῶν σεβομένων προσηλύτων τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ τῷ Βαρνάβᾳ οἵτινες προσλαλοῦντες αὐτοῖς ἔπειθον αὐτοὺς προσμένειν τῇ χάριτι τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: On the following Sabbath, nearly the whole city gathered to hear the word of the Lord.
passages.sermon: The next Sabbath day arrived.\r\nAlmost everyone in the city came together.\r\nThey gathered to hear the word of the Lord.
passages.original: Τῷ δὲ ἐρχομένῳ σαββάτῳ σχεδὸν πᾶσα ἡ πόλις συνήχθη ἀκοῦσαι τὸν λόγον τοῦ κυρίου

passages.text: But when the Jews saw the crowds, they were filled with jealousy, and they blasphemously contradicted what Paul was saying.
passages.sermon:
The Jews saw the crowds.
They became very jealous.
They spoke against what Paul was saying.
They spoke in a blasphemous way.
passages.original: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι τοὺς ὄχλους ἐπλήσθησαν ζήλου καὶ ἀντέλεγον τοῖς ὑπὸ Παύλου λαλουμένοις βλασφημοῦντες

passages.text: Then Paul and Barnabas answered them boldly: “It was necessary to speak the word of God to you first. But since you reject it and do not consider yourselves worthy of eternal life, we now turn to the Gentiles.
passages.sermon:
Paul and Barnabas spoke boldly.
They answered the Jews.
They said, “We had to speak the word of God to you first.
You reject this word.
You do not consider yourselves worthy of eternal life.
Now we turn to the Gentiles.”
passages.original: Παρρησιασάμενοί τε ὁ Παῦλος καὶ ὁ Βαρνάβας εἶπαν Ὑμῖν ἦν ἀναγκαῖον πρῶτον λαληθῆναι τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐπειδὴ ἀπωθεῖσθε αὐτὸν καὶ οὐκ ἀξίους κρίνετε ἑαυτοὺς τῆς αἰωνίου ζωῆς ἰδοὺ στρεφόμεθα εἰς τὰ ἔθνη

passages.text: For this is what the Lord has commanded us: ‘I have made you a light for the Gentiles, to bring salvation to the ends of the earth.’”
passages.sermon:
The Lord gave us a command.
He said, “I have made you a light for the Gentiles.”
You will bring salvation.
You will bring it to the ends of the earth.
passages.original: οὕτως γὰρ ἐντέταλται ἡμῖν ὁ Κύριος Τέθεικά σε εἰς φῶς ἐθνῶν τοῦ εἶναί σε εἰς σωτηρίαν ἕως ἐσχάτου τῆς γῆς

passages.text: When the Gentiles heard this, they rejoiced and glorified the word of the Lord, and all who were appointed for eternal life believed.
passages.sermon:
The Gentiles heard this message.
They rejoiced.
They glorified the word of the Lord.
All who were appointed for eternal life believed.
passages.original: Ἀκούοντα δὲ τὰ ἔθνη ἔχαιρον καὶ ἐδόξαζον τὸν λόγον τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ ἐπίστευσαν ὅσοι ἦσαν τεταγμένοι εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον

passages.text: And the word of the Lord spread throughout that region.
passages.sermon: The word of the Lord spread.\r\nIt spread throughout that region.
passages.original: διεφέρετο δὲ ὁ λόγος τοῦ Κυρίου δι’ ὅλης τῆς χώρας

passages.text: The Jews, however, incited the religious women of prominence and the leading men of the city. They stirred up persecution against Paul and Barnabas and drove them out of their district.
passages.sermon:
The Jews acted first.
They incited the prominent women who were religious.
They also incited the leading men of the city.
The Jews stirred up persecution against Paul and Barnabas.
They drove Paul and Barnabas out of their district.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ Ἰουδαῖοι παρώτρυναν τὰς σεβομένας γυναῖκας τὰς εὐσχήμονας καὶ τοὺς πρώτους τῆς πόλεως καὶ ἐπήγειραν διωγμὸν ἐπὶ τὸν Παῦλον καὶ Βαρνάβαν καὶ ἐξέβαλον αὐτοὺς ἀπὸ τῶν ὁρίων αὐτῶν

passages.text: So they shook the dust off their feet in protest against them and went to Iconium.
passages.sermon:
Paul and Barnabas faced persecution in that region.
They left the area.
They shook the dust off their feet against those people.
They went to Iconium.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ ἐκτιναξάμενοι τὸν κονιορτὸν τῶν ποδῶν ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς ἦλθον εἰς Ἰκόνιον

passages.text: And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.
passages.sermon:
The disciples followed Jesus Christ.
The disciples trusted in Him.
God filled the disciples with joy.
God filled the disciples with the Holy Spirit.
passages.original: οἵ τε μαθηταὶ ἐπληροῦντο χαρᾶς καὶ Πνεύματος Ἁγίου
